_what_this_is: PRE-REGISTERED FORWARD TEST of a $250 HARD DAILY LOSS LIMIT on the tournament gates. Registered 2026-09-13 BEFORE any forward session, because the level was chosen on 43 historical sessions and is therefore overfit until proven forward.
registered_by: operator: 'run the $250 daily loss limit forward from tonight'

why.losses_are_single_session_dominated: single-lot book, 43 sessions: worst day -$817 against a median losing day of -$242 = 3.4x, and THE FIVE WORST DAYS ARE 52% OF ALL LOSS
why.retrospective_effect: applying a $250 limit takes the book from +$35/day to +$87/day; a $400 limit gives +$62/day
why.it_needs_no_edge: a loss limit cannot create expectancy. It truncates the left tail of the DAILY distribution. That is why it is the highest-value change available and why it is testable without a signal.
why.external_support: every professional hard rule in the industry is on LOSS, never on win rate or target (6 independent traditions). Topstep's own figure: 'over 63% of traders have lost account in a single day.'

\u26a0_the_honest_caveat: THE $250 WAS SELECTED ON THE SAME 43 SESSIONS IT IS SCORED ON. Tighter limits looked MONOTONICALLY better in backtest ($200 gave +$4,326), and a monotone improvement to the tightest value tested usually means 'stop trading' is the optimum - which is exactly the shape that does not survive forward. The level is frozen here precisely so that cannot be re-fitted.

the_rule.session: the CME session, 22:00Z reopen to 22:00Z - NOT the calendar day. A midnight reset would clear the limit mid-session, which is the one moment it must not.
the_rule.action: bench all six tournament gates. It writes `off` and NEVER `on` - asserted against the source by tests/test_daily_loss_limit.py
the_rule.self_clearing: gazbot7-gate-reactivate arms every `off` gate at 22:00Z, so a bench lasts exactly one session. This is deliberate: the desk has been bitten by a protective mechanism that disarmed the desk it was protecting and needed a human to undo.
the_rule.cadence: every 2 minutes, offset off the router's 5-minute write and the reconciler's 30s tick

what_is_recorded_every_session: whether the limit fired, and at what time and trade count
the P&L the session went on to make AFTER the fire time (the counterfactual: what the limit saved or cost)

verdict_rule.primary: mean $/session WITH the limit beats mean $/session WITHOUT it (the counterfactual, reconstructed from the trades that would have followed), day-clustered 95% CI on the difference excluding zero
verdict_rule.expected_fire_rate: about 6 of 43 sessions historically, so ~8 fires in 60 - and THAT IS THE PROBLEM WITH THIS TEST: the evidence accrues only on the days it fires. Expect INCONCLUSIVE and report it as such.
verdict_rule.REFUTED: the limit costs money forward - i.e. sessions it truncated would have recovered
verdict_rule._not_required: statistical significance. This is a risk rule, not an edge. If it is merely neutral on P&L and cuts the worst day, that is a PASS on its own terms.

rules_of_engagement: DO NOT move the $250. A changed level restarts the count at zero.
DO NOT add a second condition (time of day, trade count, gate).
DO NOT extend it to the rider without a separate decision - the rider is the desk's only automatic protection path and a loss limit that silences it is the cross-desk-kill failure again.
Read the interim only to check it FIRED correctly, never to judge it.
